Project overview

  • Client: Reply (Internal Product / Global Launch)
  • Sector: Enterprise B2B Consulting / E-commerce
  • Timeline: July 2020 – July 2021 (Global Launch September 2021)
  • Team: 2 Front-End Developers (including myself), 2 Backend Developers, 1 Project Manager, 1 Business Analyst, 1 Dedicated QA Tester
  • Core skills demonstrated: Front-end engineering (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript), UI/UX system design, e-commerce integration (Shopware APIs), enterprise authentication (Azure SSO), responsive web architecture

What this project proves about me: I bridge complex enterprise backends and intuitive user interfaces, translating intricate business requirements and third-party APIs into clean, accessible, and high-performance commercial front-ends under strict delivery deadlines.

The challenge

Consulting engagements have traditionally relied on prolonged sales cycles, opaque pricing, and manual scoping meetings. Reply aimed to disrupt this pattern by launching ROSe (Reply Online Services)—a self-service B2B consulting marketplace allowing corporate clients to bypass intermediaries and purchase fixed-outcome consulting modules directly from domain specialists in Cloud, AI, and Cybersecurity.

From an engineering and interface perspective, the platform faced several acute constraints:

  1. Abstract service catalogue: Unlike physical products, consulting sessions represent variable-time, expert-led services that require clear scoping, prerequisite definition, and real-time scheduling.
  2. Enterprise-grade security requirements: Access had to integrate seamlessly into corporate identity providers via Microsoft Azure Single Sign-On (SSO) without adding friction to the checkout path.
  3. Tight delivery window: The commercial imperative demanded a fully functioning beta within six months, progressing swiftly to a modular, editorial-style production release capable of scaling internationally.

My process

I followed a structured development and UX process aligned with our two-week sprint Agile cadence:

  1. Requirements scoping and architectural alignment: Collaborated with the Project Manager, Business Analyst, and backend engineers to evaluate Shopware headless API endpoints, authenticate data flows, and establish responsive UI performance targets.
  2. Beta prototyping and proof-of-concept: Built the foundational front-end client to validate end-to-end booking logic, integrate the Azure SSO flow, and embed an AI concierge bot prototype.
  3. Quality assurance and cross-browser testing: Ran structured cross-device validation alongside the dedicated QA tester, resolving layout regressions, view transitions, and accessibility compliance issues.
  4. Editorial redesign and component refactoring: Scaled the platform post-beta by executing an "Editorial Style" visual redesign, establishing reusable CSS/JS component modules, multi-session scheduling logic, and support ticketing workflows.
  5. Production deployment and performance tuning: Optimised bundle sizes, minified critical assets, and verified cross-browser compatibility across legacy enterprise browsers and modern mobile viewports ahead of global launch.

What I did

As the core front-end engineer on the squad, I was responsible for transforming wireframes and system requirements into production-ready code:

Phase 1: Foundational Beta Architecture

I developed the initial client-facing prototype from scratch, focusing on transactional integrity and authentication. I built responsive component shells that consumed Shopware service APIs, allowing users to browse service tiers, inspect expert profiles, and complete test checkout journeys.

Demonstration of the early beta environment showing core booking interaction flows and prototype conversational concierge logic.

I also handled the front-end presentation logic for the interactive AI concierge bot. The bot parsed inbound natural-language queries to return direct links to relevant consulting packages, reducing navigation overhead for prospective clients searching for specialised technical capabilities.

Phase 2: Editorial Redesign & Feature Expansion

Following beta feedback, I collaborated with a full-stack developer to execute a major front-end overhaul. We shifted the visual identity from a transactional utility to an authoritative, magazine-inspired "Editorial Style" marketplace designed to build credibility with senior procurement leaders and technology directors.

  • Advanced multi-session scheduling: Built stateful interface logic allowing clients to schedule multiple workshops simultaneously, resolving time-zone variations and consultant availability states.
  • Support ecosystem: Developed an integrated FAQ accordion architecture and a streamlined ticket submission system to capture post-consultation requirements directly within the user account area.
  • Modular component refactoring: Rebuilt the legacy layout engine using modern semantic HTML5, modular CSS3, and native JavaScript components to ensure zero layout shift, low bundle weight, and rapid rendering on corporate networks.

The Phase 2 desktop interface: featuring a high-impact gradient hero unit, structured three-column value propositions, and a modular card grid organising multi-disciplinary consulting workshops.

Why I made these decisions

  • Shopware API decoupling: Rather than relying entirely on default server-rendered Shopware templates, I prioritised custom, lightweight front-end templates. This prevented bloat, ensured fine-grained control over accessibility and CSS architecture, and delivered faster load times across corporate proxy networks.
  • Modular component design over monolithic views: Structured layout elements (cards, booking panels, modals) as isolated modules. This modular approach accelerated our velocity during the Phase 2 editorial redesign, allowing us to restructure the home and catalogue pages without breaking booking dependencies.
  • Enterprise-first SSO placement: Placed Azure SSO entry points directly inside checkout and scheduling flows rather than behind a generic barrier, minimising authentication drop-off while satisfying enterprise data governance.
  • Information density in the catalogue: Shifted the catalogue grid to provide visible metadata (delivery timeframe, target audience, session prerequisites) directly on cards, reducing the need for users to open multiple browser tabs to compare consulting modules.

Impact / results

  • On-time global launch: Delivered the production-ready platform within the contracted six-month timeline, launching internationally in September 2021.
  • Industry press coverage: Featured prominently in European technology press, including 01net, highlighting Reply's transition toward AI-driven, accessible digital services.
  • Enterprise adoption: Successfully processed direct enterprise consultation transactions across diverse business units, establishing a repeatable direct-to-consumer consulting channel for Reply specialists.

Tools and skills applied

Category Tools / skills
Front-End Development HTML5, CSS3 (BEM / Modular), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Responsive Web Design
E-Commerce & Architecture Shopware API integration, Headless e-commerce concepts, RESTful Web APIs
Authentication & Cloud Microsoft Azure Single Sign-On (Azure SSO), Enterprise IAM workflows
Agile & Delivery Jira, Git/GitHub, Sprint planning, Cross-functional collaboration, QA bug tracking

Roles performed on this project

  • Front-End Developer: Owned component architecture, markup structure, responsive styling, and client-side integration with Shopware and Azure SSO.
  • UI/UX Contributor: Partnered with full-stack developers and business analysts to adapt and implement the Phase 2 editorial visual design system and multi-session booking patterns.

childMarkdownRemark.html: Reply needed an enterprise-grade digital marketplace, ROSe (Reply Online Services), to allow corporate clients to directly browse, configure, and book interactive consulting sessions across artificial intelligence, cloud, and cybersecurity. Operating within an Agile squad, I was responsible for the front-end architecture and UI implementation, translating complex service-booking requirements into a modular, responsive web application. Working across a rapid six-month delivery cycle, I integrated custom front-end interfaces with a headless Shopware e-commerce engine, implemented Microsoft Azure Single Sign-On (SSO) for corporate authentication, and developed the front-end container for an AI concierge. Following an initial beta, I led an editorial redesign and feature expansion, introducing multi-session scheduling and structured support ecosystems. The platform launched globally in September 2021, earning coverage in European technology publications such as 01net.
